title: Customer Cohort by First Order Month
description:
Group customers into monthly **cohorts** based on the month of their first ever order. Return cohort month and customer count.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

Output columns: `cohort_year`, `cohort_month`, `customer_count`. Order by `cohort_year`, `cohort_month`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-10','completed',100.00),(2,2,DATE '2026-01-20','completed',200.00),(3,1,DATE '2026-02-05','completed',150.00),(4,3,DATE '2026-02-15','completed',300.00),(5,4,DATE '2026-02-25','completed',250.00),(6,5,DATE '2026-03-05','completed',180.00);
solution_sql: WITH first_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM first_order_date) AS cohort_year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM first_order_date) AS cohort_month, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM first_orders GROUP BY cohort_year, cohort_month ORDER BY cohort_year, cohort_month

test_cases.description: Jan cohort: 2 customers; Feb cohort: 2; Mar cohort: 1

hints: MIN(order_date) per customer gives their first order date.
Group by cohort year+month to count customers per cohort.
explanation: The CTE finds each customer's first order via MIN(). Grouping by year+month of that first date creates cohorts. Customer 1 first ordered in January (so did customer 2). Customers 3 and 4 first ordered in February. Customer 5 first ordered in March.
